questions.q: When does Git perform a fast-forward merge instead of creating a merge commit?
options: Whenever you pass the --force flag
When the target branch (e.g. main) hasn't moved since the feature branch was created, so its pointer can simply move forward
Only when there's a merge conflict
Every time you run git merge, with no exceptions
questions.explain: A fast-forward is possible only when the branch being merged into hasn't diverged — Git can just slide its pointer forward to match, with no new commit needed.

questions.q: What makes a merge commit different from an ordinary commit?
options: It has no parent commit at all
It can only be created by an administrator
It has two parent commits, one from each branch being combined
It deletes one of the two branches automatically
questions.explain: A merge commit is the result of a three-way merge and uniquely has two parents — the tip of each branch being combined — which is how both lines of history join back into one.

questions.q: Why is it good practice to run git pull on main right before merging a feature branch into it?
options: It's required by Git and the merge will fail without it
It ensures you're merging into main's current state, reducing the chance of an unexpected divergence or conflict
It automatically deletes the feature branch
It skips the need to write a commit message
questions.explain: Pulling first makes sure main reflects everyone else's latest work before you merge into it, which is exactly what avoids merging against a stale, already-diverged copy of main.

options: Prevents any merge from ever completing
Forces a merge commit to be created even when a fast-forward would otherwise be possible
Automatically resolves all merge conflicts
Deletes the branch being merged
questions.explain: --no-ff forces Git to create a merge commit rather than fast-forwarding, which some teams use so a feature's history stays visibly grouped in the log instead of being flattened.

options: Two branches are merged that have no common ancestor
Both branches changed the exact same lines of the exact same file in incompatible ways
You forget to run git init first
A branch is deleted before being merged
questions.explain: Git can combine two diverged branches' changes automatically as long as they don't overlap — a conflict arises specifically when both sides touched the same lines, which Lesson 8 covers in depth.
